slice_result.tested_scope: Read-only connector-schema inspection of the currently Chat-exposed HeyGen direct/batch video-generation mutation inputs and their exact/list/delete read surfaces, including create_video_batch, create_video_from_avatar, create_video_from_image, create_video_from_studio, create_video_from_cinematic_avatar, get_video, list_videos, and delete_video. No HeyGen account data was read and no HeyGen mutation was executed. No public-web semantic read was used.
observations: The video-creation schemas expose optional callback_id/callbackId only as a caller-defined identifier echoed in webhook payloads; the schema does not state or enforce uniqueness or idempotency for creation.
The inspected creation inputs expose no caller-controlled server-enforced idempotency key or unique operation key that the Chat tool can bind before the write.
Exact get/delete surfaces require a server-generated videoId returned after creation. A lost creation response therefore loses the exact server identity needed for deterministic reconciliation.
list_videos can filter by folderId or title substring, but it exposes no exact lookup by the precommitted callback_id and neither field is a server-enforced unique idempotency identity.
slice_result.counterexample: A create request can commit server-side and its response can be lost. Replaying the same Chat-exposed create call with the same callback_id is not specified as idempotent, while exact get/delete require the unavailable post-response videoId. Therefore the connector-visible schema cannot guarantee exactly-once reconciliation for an ambiguous write.
slice_result.current_candidate_idempotency: fail: no caller-controlled server-enforced pre-write operation identity in the Chat-exposed creation schema
slice_result.current_candidate_exact_readback: fail: exact lookup requires post-response videoId and list_videos does not resolve exact callback_id identity
